It also injects CSS styles including a base64-encoded embedded font via a data URI, modifying page appearance without network or file operations, facilitating enhanced navigation but not performing any network, file, or system sensitive operations.
slice_results.explanation: [LLM Judgment: Benign] The provided code is a well-known open-source library (AnchorJS) designed to enhance webpage navigation by adding anchor links to header elements. It operates entirely within the DOM, creating elements, assigning IDs, and injecting CSS styles including a base64-encoded font embedded via data URI. There is no network activity, no dynamic script injection, no obfuscation, no data exfiltration, and no system or file operations. The known malicious patterns from the knowledge base involve dynamic injection of remote scripts from attacker-controlled sources, obfuscation, and attempts to load trojanized payloads, none of which are present here. The code's behavior is consistent with legitimate UI enhancement and accessibility improvements, not malware.

#!/usr/bin/env bash

{ # this ensures the entire script is downloaded #

nvm_has() {
  type "$1" > /dev/null 2>&1
}

nvm_install_dir() {
  printf %s "${NVM_DIR:-"$HOME/.nvm"}"
}

nvm_latest_version() {
  echo "v0.33.8"
}

nvm_profile_is_bash_or_zsh() {
  local TEST_PROFILE
  TEST_PROFILE="${1-}"
  case "${TEST_PROFILE-}" in
    *"/.bashrc" | *"/.bash_profile" | *"/.zshrc")
      return
    ;;
    *)
      return 1
    ;;
  esac
}

nvm_source() {
  local NVM_METHOD
  NVM_METHOD="$1"
  local NVM_SOURCE_URL
  NVM_SOURCE_URL="$NVM_SOURCE"
  if [ "_$NVM_METHOD" = "_script-nvm-exec" ]; then
    NVM_SOURCE_URL="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/creationix/nvm/$(nvm_latest_version)/nvm-exec"
  elif [ "_$NVM_METHOD" = "_script-nvm-bash-completion" ]; then
    NVM_SOURCE_URL="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/creationix/nvm/$(nvm_latest_version)/bash_completion"
  elif [ -z "$NVM_SOURCE_URL" ]; then
    if [ "_$NVM_METHOD" = "_script" ]; then
      NVM_SOURCE_URL="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/creationix/nvm/$(nvm_latest_version)/nvm.sh"
    elif [ "_$NVM_METHOD" = "_git" ] || [ -z "$NVM_METHOD" ]; then
      NVM_SOURCE_URL="https://github.com/creationix/nvm.git"
    else
      echo >&2 "Unexpected value \"$NVM_METHOD\" for \$NVM_METHOD"
      return 1
    fi
  fi
  echo "$NVM_SOURCE_URL"
}

nvm_download() {
  if nvm_has "curl"; then
    curl --compressed -q "$@"
  elif nvm_has "wget"; then
    ARGS=$(echo "$*" | command sed -e 's/--progress-bar /--progress=bar /' \
                           -e 's/-L //' \
                           -e 's/--compressed //' \
                           -e 's/-I /--server-response /' \
                           -e 's/-s /-q /' \
                           -e 's/-o /-O /' \
                           -e 's/-C - /-c /')
    eval wget $ARGS
  fi
}

install_nvm_from_git() {
  local INSTALL_DIR
  INSTALL_DIR="$(nvm_install_dir)"

  if [ -d "$INSTALL_DIR/.git" ]; then
    echo "=> nvm is already installed in $INSTALL_DIR, trying to update using git"
    command printf "\r=> "
    command git --git-dir="$INSTALL_DIR"/.git --work-tree="$INSTALL_DIR" fetch origin tag "$(nvm_latest_version)" --depth=1 2> /dev/null || {
      echo >&2 "Failed to update nvm, run 'git fetch' in $INSTALL_DIR yourself."
      exit 1
    }
  else
    echo "=> Downloading nvm from git to '$INSTALL_DIR'"
    command printf "\r=> "
    mkdir -p "${INSTALL_DIR}"
    if [ "$(ls -A "${INSTALL_DIR}")" ]; then
      command git init "${INSTALL_DIR}" || {
        echo >&2 'Failed to initialize nvm repo. Please report this!'
        exit 2
      }
      command git --git-dir="${INSTALL_DIR}/.git" remote add origin "$(nvm_source)" 2> /dev/null \
        || command git --git-dir="${INSTALL_DIR}/.git" remote set-url origin "$(nvm_source)" || {
        echo >&2 'Failed to add remote "origin" (or set the URL). Please report this!'
        exit 2
      }
      command git --git-dir="${INSTALL_DIR}/.git" fetch origin tag "$(nvm_latest_version)" --depth=1 || {
        echo >&2 'Failed to fetch origin with tags. Please report this!'
        exit 2
      }
    else
      command git clone "$(nvm_source)" -b "$(nvm_latest_version)" --depth=1 "${INSTALL_DIR}" || {
        echo >&2 'Failed to clone nvm repo. Please report this!'
        exit 2
      }
    fi
  fi
  command git --git-dir="$INSTALL_DIR"/.git --work-tree="$INSTALL_DIR" checkout -f --quiet "$(nvm_latest_version)"
  if [ ! -z "$(command git --git-dir="$INSTALL_DIR"/.git --work-tree="$INSTALL_DIR" show-ref refs/heads/master)" ]; then
    if command git --git-dir="$INSTALL_DIR"/.git --work-tree="$INSTALL_DIR" branch --quiet 2>/dev/null; then
      command git --git-dir="$INSTALL_DIR"/.git --work-tree="$INSTALL_DIR" branch --quiet -D master >/dev/null 2>&1
    else
      echo >&2 "Your version of git is out of date. Please update it!"
      command git --git-dir="$INSTALL_DIR"/.git --work-tree="$INSTALL_DIR" branch -D master >/dev/null 2>&1
    fi
  fi

  echo "=> Compressing and cleaning up git repository"
  if ! command git --git-dir="$INSTALL_DIR"/.git --work-tree="$INSTALL_DIR" reflog expire --expire=now --all; then
    echo >&2 "Your version of git is out of date. Please update it!"
  fi
  if ! command git --git-dir="$INSTALL_DIR"/.git --work-tree="$INSTALL_DIR" gc --auto --aggressive --prune=now ; then
    echo >&2 "Your version of git is out of date. Please update it!"
  fi
  return
}

install_nvm_as_script() {
  local INSTALL_DIR
  INSTALL_DIR="$(nvm_install_dir)"
  local NVM_SOURCE_LOCAL
  NVM_SOURCE_LOCAL="$(nvm_source script)"
  local NVM_EXEC_SOURCE
  NVM_EXEC_SOURCE="$(nvm_source script-nvm-exec)"
  local NVM_BASH_COMPLETION_SOURCE
  NVM_BASH_COMPLETION_SOURCE="$(nvm_source script-nvm-bash-completion)"

  mkdir -p "$INSTALL_DIR"
  if [ -f "$INSTALL_DIR/nvm.sh" ]; then
    echo "=> nvm is already installed in $INSTALL_DIR, trying to update the script"
  else
    echo "=> Downloading nvm as script to '$INSTALL_DIR'"
  fi
  nvm_download -s "$NVM_SOURCE_LOCAL" -o "$INSTALL_DIR/nvm.sh" || {
    echo >&2 "Failed to download '$NVM_SOURCE_LOCAL'"
    return 1
  } &
  nvm_download -s "$NVM_EXEC_SOURCE" -o "$INSTALL_DIR/nvm-exec" || {
    echo >&2 "Failed to download '$NVM_EXEC_SOURCE'"
    return 2
  } &
  nvm_download -s "$NVM_BASH_COMPLETION_SOURCE" -o "$INSTALL_DIR/bash_completion" || {
    echo >&2 "Failed to download '$NVM_BASH_COMPLETION_SOURCE'"
    return 2
  } &
  for job in $(jobs -p | sort)
  do
    wait "$job" || return $?
  done
  chmod a+x "$INSTALL_DIR/nvm-exec" || {
    echo >&2 "Failed to mark '$INSTALL_DIR/nvm-exec' as executable"
    return 3
  }
}

nvm_do_install() {
  if [ -z "${METHOD}" ]; then
    if nvm_has git; then
      install_nvm_from_git
    elif nvm_has nvm_download; then
      install_nvm_as_script
    else

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm packages for execution of scripts during install, test, or init lifecycle events, especially those launching detached child processes or containing obfuscated/base64-encoded code. Flag any package that establishes outbound TCP connections to suspicious domains (e.g., rsh.51pwn.com) or uncommon ports during or after installation. Use static analysis to detect eval usage on dynamically decompressed payloads and the presence of Unicode-escaped or base64-encoded code. Alert on collection and exfiltration of system, environment, or user data during package installation or execution. Correlate file indicators (scripts/init.js, scripts/rsh.js, suspicious package.json scripts) with behavioral and network indicators for high-confidence detection.

Its presence in projects is unintentional and could be abused in the future if the package contents change to include malicious code. The risk is that such packages can be silently included in builds, creating a potential supply chain attack vector by providing an opportunity for attackers to later introduce malicious payloads into a widely distributed, trusted dependency.

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan package.json and package-lock.json for dependencies with suspicious names such as '-', 'i', 'g', or names matching npm command flags. Flag packages that have no functional code or only export null/empty modules in their main files. Check for non-functional npm scripts referencing missing files. Monitor for sudden inclusion of such packages in projects, especially if not explicitly added by developers, and alert on high download counts for packages with no legitimate usage or documentation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code contains an extensive list of environment variable checks specifically targeting known sandbox, CI/CD, and analysis environments. This is a strong indicator of evasion tactics, which are rarely present in legitimate packages.

malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate software may check for CI/CD or test environments to adjust logging or behavior, but not to suppress core functionality or evade detection. The use of a large, frequently updated filter list is not typical in benign code.

detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages that access and exfiltrate environment variables, especially those making HTTP POST requests to known malicious domains such as pipedream.net subdomains. Flag packages containing large environment variable filter lists or obfuscated code in build.js or similar files. Pay special attention to packages with multiple high-numbered versions and a benign latest version, as this is a common evasion technique. Use both static and dynamic analysis to inspect all package versions, not just the latest, and correlate network activity with package installation or import events.

package_info.why_malicious: These packages are malicious at a macro level because they are mass-generated, empty, or garbage packages published solely to exploit the Tea.xyz crypto protocol's rewards system. This activity pollutes public package registries, creates unnecessary maintenance burdens, and disrupts the open source ecosystem, even though the packages do not contain traditional malware or direct code-based threats.

attack_chain.leads_to: Mass publication of spam packages to public registries.

package_info.why_malicious: The package is part of a coordinated supply chain attack campaign by LofyGang, designed to steal sensitive information such as Discord tokens, credit card data, and streaming/gaming account credentials. The campaign leverages techniques including typosquatting, starjacking, sub-dependency hiding, and persistent malware to evade detection and maintain access. The package modifies files in the Discord installation directory to intercept and exfiltrate sensitive data to attacker-controlled Discord webhooks.
